newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria sets up water council to battle drought.
newsitem.headline: Algeria sets up water council to battle drought.

text.p: Algeria has set up a task force to draw up a programme of water rationing and battle waste to counter drought threatening its agriculture, the government newspaper El Moudjahid said on Monday.
Rainfall coinciding with the most sensitive growing period for cereals and other crops is 70 percent below average, according to a ministerial report.

The newspaper said water supplies for Algiers, Oran and Constantine cities have reached critical level. Residents in the capital Algiers say that for several weeks water has been distributed one day in every two, while some regions receive it only one day in three.

El Moudjahid said waste and leaks in the water distribution system reached around 40 percent of total water used. It said that on March 22 -- World Water Day -- there were 100,000 calls for water repairs throughout Algeria.
The North African country harvested a record 4.9 million tonnes of cereals in the 1995-96 season, compared with 2.13 million tonnes in the 1994-95 season.
Trade experts estimate Algeria's grain imports in the year to June 30, 1996 at 4.1 million tonnes for wheat and 1.1 million tonnes for other cereals.

Harvesting in southern Algeria usually starts in late May and late June in other parts of the country. El Moudjahid said cereals were the most threatened crops because they relied mostly on rainfall, rather than irrigation.
Algeria is one of the world's main importers of hard wheat to feed its 29 million people.
